why: The AUTHORED half of a feature-ledger row. l6-parity-rows.cjs derives every MEASURED field from a cat6 run artifact and refuses to invent any of these; a spec row id with no entry here refuses BY NAME rather than being written with a guessed route. One block per app, keyed by the row ids in probes/l6-parity.js.
howToAddAnApp: Read the app.s SPECS block in probes/l6-parity.js for its row ids, then write one entry per id. The two destination strings and noLiquidReason are per-app, not per-row.

provenance.dictionary: Copied MECHANICALLY out of the seven dictionary rows already in parity-ledger.json (written by hand on 2026-08-17), in the spec.s own id order, by a one-off node read of the ledger -- not retyped. CORRECTED 2026-09-02: this note used to claim the seventh row, "Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close", had NO spec id and was "deliberately absent". That was false -- `l6-parity.js` declares `{ id: 'windowLifecycle', f: lifecycle }` for every app, and the live run refused BY NAME on it, which is the refusal working. Its four authored fields are now copied from that same ledger row. This block is a REGRESSION TEST -- a live cat6 dictionary run must re-derive these SEVEN features and add ZERO new rows, because the ledger already holds them under the same app-plus-feature keys. Measured 2026-09-02 at 1ec440ab: 7 rows, statuses {both: 7}, added 0.
provenance.calendar: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, and it is the first app whose block was NOT back-derived from an existing ledger row -- parity-ledger.json had no calendar row at all, so all five are new and `added` is expected to be 5, not 0. Every `currentRoute` names the selector the spec.s own `f()` reads, so the authored half cannot drift from the measured half without the run failing. `dataStateOwner` read from src/renderer/calendar.ts (LS_KEYS.calendarEvents in localStorage, mirrored to IDB_KEYS.calendarEvents) and CalendarContent.tsx (mode / cursor / modal are component state, not persisted). Liquid destination read from calendarLiquid.css and the two LiquidSurface call sites at CalendarContent.tsx:391 and :403.
provenance.settings: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, second app with no prior ledger row -- all seven are new. Every currentRoute names the selector the spec.s own f() reads. dataStateOwner separates persisted from not: advancedDisclosure is the only settings row here that survives a reopen (renderer/settingsAdvanced.ts, localStorage jp-settings-advanced-v1), while page, query and scroll are component state. Liquid destination read from the ContextualSurface call sites in SettingsNav.tsx (45, 46, 65, 69) and SettingsApp.tsx:604, and from the pane at SettingsApp.tsx:596-600 which is NOT wrapped.
provenance.scraper: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, third app with no prior ledger row -- all seven are new. Every currentRoute names the selector the spec's own f() reads, so the authored half cannot drift from the measured half without the run failing. dataStateOwner separates the two localStorage documents this app owns: the SHELL shape (page, rail, drawerOpen, drawerCategory) in renderer/scraperShellStore.ts under jp-scraper-shell-v1, and the SETTINGS values in renderer/scraperSettingsStore.ts under jp-scraper-settings-v1. reverseControls is authored against the DISCLOSURE, not against aria-pressed, because the aria-pressed reading was a measured false positive fixed in ddeb97f3: with the drawer shut and advanced mode on, the old expression counted the button labelled "Advanced controls shown" (1) and scored a reversal affordance that is not on screen. Liquid destination read from the ContextualSurface call sites in ScraperTopBar.tsx:18, ScraperNav.tsx:22/34/42/53, ScraperStatusBar.tsx:25 and ScraperSettingsDrawer.tsx:248, and from the AnchorSurface anchors at ScraperSearch.tsx:89 and ScraperSettingsDrawer.tsx:261/:319.
provenance.resources: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, fourth app with no prior ledger row. SEVEN of its eight rows were written; `collectedSections` was DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN and its metadata entry is kept anyway so a later profile with collected tools writes it without re-authoring. The reason is a repair in the same commit: its mutation targets `.mytool-card .mytool-remove` and nothing is collected on this profile, so the mutation REFUSED rather than ran. cat6 used to score that identically to a mutation that ran and flipped the wrong row, which VOIDed a run whose other 7 mutations were exact; it now reports `armed: false` and `l6-parity-rows.cjs` skips exactly that row by name. Discriminating control, live: an ARMED-but-wrong mutation (catalogueCount re-pointed at `.res-name`, which flips `resourceCards` instead) still VOIDs the whole run, so the relaxation cannot wave a broken control through. dataStateOwner is three different owners here and they are not interchangeable: the catalogue is a STATIC module (renderer/data/resources.ts), the bundle checklists are localStorage under `resources.checklist.<id>`, and the collected tools are a MAIN-PROCESS store reached through window.api.toolsList (shared/collectedTools.ts), shared with Blanc. Liquid destination read from resourcesLiquid.css, whose `:is(.fwin.fwin-liquid, .popout-root.popout-liquid)` rules touch only `.res-command-surface` and its children.
provenance.city: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, fifth app with no prior ledger row, and the FIRST written through the harness's `noLiquid` branch -- so all nine rows are `pending` by derivation, not by omission: there is no Liquid half to compare, and `pending` is the vocabulary’s own word for that. `noLiquidReason` is a MEASUREMENT, not an excuse: `liquidAbsence` reports targetHasLiquidControl false with targetChromeButtons 3 and presentation `standard`, while Resources open beside it DOES render `.fwin-b-liquid` -- the same query over every open window at the same instant, which is what separates "this window has no toggle" from "no window has one". The round trip is minimize -> restore through the taskbar (the taskbar button is a toggle, so the harness drives it twice) and `rankHeld` was true. All NINE mutations armed and each flipped exactly its own row. dataStateOwner names two separate localStorage documents: `jp-reading-garden-v1` (renderer/readingGardenProgress.ts -- stage, pagesRead, bankedPages) and `jp-mooncap-music-v1` (components/reading-garden/mooncapMusic.ts -- the ambient music choice and volume). The dossier itself is component state and correctly does not survive a reopen.
provenance.shell: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 (primary2) from source, the SIXTH app with no prior ledger row and the first whose subject is the container rather than a hosted window: `shq` excludes everything inside `.fwin`, so a taskbar of 12 buttons is not confused with a desktop of 300 controls. The harness does NOT raise this host -- there is no window to raise -- and POSTs `/focus` instead. RUN ON `wired-archive`, DELIBERATELY: `shellIdentity` is a material row and the base theme stamps no material set, so on `study-os` that row is `na` and the other eight would have been the whole ledger. The run that wrote these rows scored 9/9 in BOTH presentations with all 8 mutations armed. THE ROW WAS REPAIRED FIRST (d9f1c213) and the repair has its own cross-material control: `frutiger-aero` also PASSes 10/10, carrying `shellIdentity` by `materialStartMenu=1` with `identityElements=0`, while `wired-archive` carries it by `identityElements=2` AND `materialStartMenu=1` -- two materials, two different pieces of evidence, one row. Before the repair the same spec on `frutiger-aero` failed that row outright (`indexOf` 9 not 0; zero `aero-`prefixed elements in the shell against 178 inside a hosted window) and its mutation was UNARMABLE. dataStateOwner names three separate stores and they are not interchangeable: the main-process desktop layout snapshot (renderer/desktopState.ts -- windows, icons, z-order, active desktop), localStorage `jp-os-desktop-prefs-v1` (renderer/desktopPrefs.ts -- clock format) and localStorage `jp-os-theme` (renderer/theme/engine.ts -- the material stamp).
provenance.blancShell: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 (primary2) from source, the SEVENTH app with no prior ledger row and the SECOND shell — a separate BrowserWindow (`blanc.html?blanc=1`) hosting 0 `.fwin`, reached with `--win blanc`. Its presentation axis is chrome reduction (`is-taskbar-hidden`), not a palette and not native fullscreen; the spec records both rejected candidates and the reasons stand. RUN: PASS 10/10, 8/8 reachable in BOTH presentations, round trip 0 diffs with an INPUT dirtied first, 8 of 8 mutations armed and each flipping exactly its own row. ONE ROW HAD TO BE REPAIRED FIRST and the defect was in the instrument, not the shell: `workspaceToggleHonest` read the fullscreen control at CHECK time and scored `control=null` -> FALSE. Measured live: the Blanc window renders exactly ONE `.blanc-icon-btn` ("Search Blanc") on the `Read` route, because the control is route-scoped by `canExpandWorkspace` (BlancShell.tsx:430). The drive visits a qualifying route and then correctly RESTORES the user's own route, so by check time the control is legitimately gone -- a deliberate product decision was reading as a lying label. The reading is now recorded where the control exists (`readNav`, route "Mine") with a second chance on the restored route, and the row is `na` naming BOTH routes if neither offers it. Its mutation falsifies the recorded label instead of the element, so it arms on exactly the runs the row can score. dataStateOwner is mostly COMPONENT state here and that is the finding worth keeping: `taskbarHidden`, `compactToolsOpen`, `masterSearchOpen` and `workspaceFull` are all unpersisted, so a reduced or fullscreen Blanc cannot be inherited by the next launch; only the route survives, and only when the user has asked Blanc to remember it (`jp-blanc-mode-v1` / `jp-blanc-memory-v1`, renderer/blancMode.ts).
provenance.games: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 (primary2) from source, the EIGHTH app with no prior ledger row. RUN: PASS 10/10, 10/10 reachable in BOTH presentations, round trip 0 diffs, 10 of 10 mutations armed and each flipping exactly its own row, 0 driven refusals -- and it was driven end to end, not merely inspected: a round was STARTED, "ro" was typed, submit moved disabled true -> false, and the round was ABORTED back to a ready state the harness then re-read. THE PROFILE IS EMPTY AND THE RUN STILL SCORES 10/10, which is the point worth recording: the previous handoff warned that an empty harness is CAPPED rather than skipped, and that is true of surfaces whose rows need rows to exist. Games is not one of them, because four of its rows are written to score HONEST EMPTY STATE rather than content -- `sourceMaterial` reads `pct=noList scaleX=0 agrees=true` with the words "No word list uploaded for this level", `exposureTracking` reads `seen=0/59` with stated and derived pct both 0 and the bar at 0, `roundHistory` reads `rows=0 complete=0` against the empty-state sentence, and `materialScope` reads `mode=auto scripts=0 groups=0 shapeHeld=true`. A bar that agrees with a zero is as real a reading as one that agrees with a 60. dataStateOwner names FIVE separate stores and they are not interchangeable: `jp-game-arena-settings-v1` (length, language, kana scope), `jp-game-arena-seen-v1` (exposure), `jp-game-progress-v1` (last 30 results + high scores), `jp-level-lists` (the word lists coverage is computed against) and renderer/levelService.ts (the level). The round session itself is deliberately unpersisted, which is what makes the abort recovery safe for a harness to drive against a real profile.

city.noLiquidReason: NONE, and it is a product fact this run measured rather than assumed. Mooncap is a frameless window: `liquidAbsence` reports `targetHasLiquidControl: false` with `targetChromeButtons: 3` (a real chrome cluster, so the absence is not a missing title bar) and `targetPresentation: "standard"`, while Resources open beside it DOES render `.fwin-b-liquid` — a discriminating control taken at the same instant over every open window. The surface is a painted scene, not a document over a material, so there is nothing for a translucent layer to sit in front of; L12 bullet 1 records the same three sections (city / musicwidget / visualizer) as having no presentation toggle. The round trip that stands in for the presentation flip is therefore minimize -> restore through the taskbar, and it held.

scenePainted.feature: The scene is actually painted: every canvas has pixels and the parallax layers are all present

heroPlacement.feature: The hero affordance is inside the window and big enough to hit
heroPlacement.currentRoute: Mooncap window > `.reading-garden-mushroom-hitbox` rect, compared against the window rect
heroPlacement.keyboardRoute: the hitbox is the keyboard route to the dossier as well as the pointer one

devOnlyIsolated.feature: Development-only affordances are marked as such and never mixed into the user controls
devOnlyIsolated.currentRoute: Mooncap window > `[data-dev-only="true"]` nodes, each of whose class names must say console/debug/dev, alongside the real `button, input, select, textarea` controls
devOnlyIsolated.keyboardRoute: not a route; it is the guarantee that the surface a user reaches contains no developer instrumentation

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close
windowLifecycle.currentRoute: Mooncap window > `.fwin-frameless-controls` chrome cluster (frameless, so the buttons live outside the usual title bar)
windowLifecycle.keyboardRoute: real buttons in the frameless control cluster

shell.standardDestination: The Study OS shell itself — `.os-desktop`: the desk surface and its icon grid, the `.os-taskbar` (start control, virtual-desktop switches, one button per hosted window, the tray and its clock) and the surfaces the taskbar discloses (`.os-start`, `.os-flyout`)
shell.liquidDestination: The SAME shell, unchanged, while a window it hosts is in Liquid. The shell is the container, not the content: the presentation axis flips a hosted `.fwin`, and every row here is scored on the desk and the taskbar OUTSIDE that window (`shq` excludes anything inside `.fwin`). That is the parity claim — a window going translucent must not cost the shell a capability, and the L2 rule that keeps dense work on stable anchors applies to the shell most of all, since the taskbar is the only route back to a window that is behind another.

taskbarIdentity.feature: One taskbar button per hosted window, each still carrying its own window's identity
taskbarIdentity.currentRoute: Taskbar > `.os-task-wins` > `.os-task-win` (one per `.fwin` the desk hosts), each with a `title` naming its window
taskbarIdentity.keyboardRoute: real `<button>`s in the taskbar's focus order; the close affordance is a child of the button, so the button itself stays the raise route
taskbarIdentity.dataStateOwner: DesktopShell's `wins` state, hydrated from the main-process desktop layout snapshot (renderer/desktopState.ts; the `jp-os-wins` localStorage key is the migrated-from legacy)

taskbarRaises.feature: The taskbar button raises its window to the top of the stack, from behind another window
taskbarRaises.currentRoute: Taskbar > `.os-task-win` for a window that is NOT already on top; the row reads the z-order rank afterwards, never the click
taskbarRaises.keyboardRoute: the same buttons, activated by Enter/Space
taskbarRaises.dataStateOwner: DesktopShell window z-order (`globalZTop` in the desktop layout snapshot) — persisted, so the stack survives a reopen. The button is a TOGGLE: one click raises or restores, a second minimises what the first brought up.

startEntryPoint.feature: The start control opens the app menu, and closes it again
startEntryPoint.currentRoute: Taskbar > `.os-start-btn` opens `.os-start`; dismissed by `.os-start-backdrop` or by the start control again
startEntryPoint.keyboardRoute: a real button that toggles a mounted surface, with a backdrop dismissal
startEntryPoint.dataStateOwner: component state (`startOpen`) in DesktopShell.tsx — not persisted, so the menu is closed on every boot

trayFlyout.feature: A tray control opens its flyout, and the same control closes it
trayFlyout.currentRoute: Taskbar > `.os-tray` > `.os-tray-btn` (Quick settings) opens `.os-flyout`; the same button closes it — `.os-panel-backdrop` was MEASURED not to dismiss it and is deliberately not used
trayFlyout.keyboardRoute: real buttons carrying `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, each with `title` and `aria-label`
trayFlyout.dataStateOwner: quick settings is a shell-level surface driven by the `shell:toggleQuickSettings` window event; tray overflow is component state (`trayOverflowOpen`) with `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`

virtualDesktops.feature: Two virtual desktops, with exactly one marked current
virtualDesktops.currentRoute: Taskbar > `.os-desktop-switches` > `.os-desktop-switch` x2, exactly one carrying `active` and `aria-pressed`
virtualDesktops.keyboardRoute: two real buttons; `aria-pressed` states which desktop you are on programmatically, not only in paint
virtualDesktops.dataStateOwner: renderer/desktopState.ts — `activeDesktopIndex` in the main-process desktop layout snapshot; switching flushes the outgoing viewport's windows and icons before hydrating the incoming one, so each desktop keeps its own

trayControls.feature: Every tray control is NAMED — an icon-only button with no accessible name is a capability the user cannot find
trayControls.currentRoute: Taskbar > `.os-tray` > `.os-tray-btn` (search, hidden icons, quick settings, the notification bell, show desktop), each read for `title` or `aria-label`
trayControls.keyboardRoute: the accessible name IS the keyboard route here: these are icon-only buttons and the name is the only thing that distinguishes them
trayControls.dataStateOwner: none — the naming is structural, from `t()` keys in DesktopShell.tsx; the show-desktop button additionally carries `aria-pressed` for its own toggled state

clock.feature: The taskbar clock reads a real time
clock.currentRoute: Taskbar > `.os-clock` (TaskbarClock), matched against `\d{1,2}:\d{2}` rather than asserted present
clock.keyboardRoute: not a control; it is the shell stating the time
clock.dataStateOwner: renderer/desktopPrefs.ts — localStorage `jp-os-desktop-prefs-v1` carries `clockSeconds`, `clock24h` and `clockShowDate`; the time itself is live and stored nowhere

shellIdentity.feature: A material theme's identity is real: the stamp belongs to the active theme and the shell renders that material's own furniture
shellIdentity.currentRoute: `<html data-materials>` + `<html data-theme>`, against shell-owned furniture — `.wired-wall-atmosphere` / `.wired-tray-lamps` (wired only, DesktopShell.tsx:2748 and :3502) and `.os-start-aero-menu`, the secret start surface BOTH material sets render (DesktopShell.tsx:683), recorded while the menu is open
shellIdentity.keyboardRoute: not a control; it is the shell's claim about which OS the user is in, checked against what it actually painted
shellIdentity.dataStateOwner: renderer/theme/engine.ts — localStorage `jp-os-theme` holds the theme id, and `applyThemeAttributes` is the single choke point that stamps `data-materials` from that theme's `materialSet`. On the base theme there is no material set, so the row is `na` rather than false.

desktopSurface.feature: The shell owns a real desk the user can drop onto, and its icon count is what the shell rendered
desktopSurface.currentRoute: `.os-desktop` rect, plus `.os-desk-icon` counted rather than asserted — an empty grid is honest state, not a failure
desktopSurface.keyboardRoute: the icons are focusable desk entries; the desk itself is a drop target, not a control
desktopSurface.dataStateOwner: renderer/desktopState.ts — `icons` per viewport in the desktop layout snapshot (legacy key `jp-os-icons`), seeded per desktop (`SEED_CITY_ICONS` for the city viewport, empty for study)

blancShell.standardDestination: The Blanc shell in its own BrowserWindow (`blanc.html?blanc=1`, BlancShell.tsx): the `.blanc-taskbar` route rail down the left, the `.blanc-top` bar with the title, clock, master search and the Context tools disclosure, and the 42 tools rendering inside `.blanc-content`. It hosts **0** `.fwin` — this is a second, separate shell, not a window on the Study OS desk.
blancShell.liquidDestination: The SAME shell with its chrome REDUCED: `.blanc-root.is-taskbar-hidden`, reached by `.blanc-taskbar-toggle` and reversed by `.blanc-taskbar-reveal`. That is this host's presentation axis and the choice is recorded rather than assumed — NOT `workspaceFull` (its handler calls `window.api.blancSetFullScreen()`, a persisted native mutation the category never asked for) and NOT dark mode (a palette swap leaves every capability where it was, so parity would be equal by construction). Hiding the taskbar removes nine routes and the exit from the screen while leaving `.blanc-content` untouched, so "is any capability lost when the chrome is reduced?" is a real question with a real reveal affordance as its answer.

taskbarIdentity.feature: One titled route per section, exactly one current, and the current one agreeing with the title the shell painted
taskbarIdentity.currentRoute: Blanc window > `.blanc-taskbar` > `.blanc-nav` > `.blanc-nav-btn` x9 (Read, Mine, Deck, Cards, Media, Stats, Toolbox, Blocks, Settings), each with a `title`, cross-checked against `.blanc-title` in the top bar
taskbarIdentity.keyboardRoute: real `<button>`s in the rail's focus order; `active` marks the current one and the painted title is the second, independent statement of the same fact
taskbarIdentity.dataStateOwner: BlancShell `tab` state, seeded from `loadBlancMode().lastTab` when `rememberLastTab` is set — localStorage `jp-blanc-mode-v1` / `jp-blanc-memory-v1` (renderer/blancMode.ts)

navRoutes.feature: Clicking a route actually changes the surface, and the shell paints the route it was asked for
navRoutes.currentRoute: Blanc window > `.blanc-nav-btn` for a route that is NOT current, read back off `.blanc-title`; the run then restores whichever route the user had open
navRoutes.keyboardRoute: the same rail buttons, activated by Enter/Space
navRoutes.dataStateOwner: BlancShell `tab` state; persisted through renderer/blancMode.ts only when the user has asked Blanc to remember the last tab, so a fresh window opens on Read

chromeRecoverable.feature: The chrome can be reduced and brought back, with the SAME routes returning — an enable with a real disable path
chromeRecoverable.currentRoute: Blanc window > `.blanc-taskbar-toggle` hides `.blanc-taskbar`; `.blanc-taskbar-reveal` (rendered only while hidden and not fullscreen) brings it back with all nine routes
chromeRecoverable.keyboardRoute: two real buttons; the reveal control is the only route back, which is why its presence is scored rather than assumed
chromeRecoverable.dataStateOwner: BlancShell `taskbarHidden` component state — deliberately NOT persisted, so a reduced shell cannot be inherited by the next launch

clock.feature: The Blanc top bar reads a real time
clock.currentRoute: Blanc window > `.blanc-clock`, matched against `\d{1,2}:\d{2}` rather than asserted present
clock.keyboardRoute: not a control; it is the shell stating the time
clock.dataStateOwner: none — live, stored nowhere. Blanc does not share the Study OS taskbar's `jp-os-desktop-prefs-v1` clock format.

masterSearch.feature: Master search: Blanc's one cross-tool capability, opened by its own control and dismissed by Escape
masterSearch.currentRoute: Blanc window > `.blanc-icon-btn` (aria-label "Search Blanc", Ctrl+F) opens `.blanc-master-search`, whose results are `#blanc-master-search-results [role="option"]`
masterSearch.keyboardRoute: a labelled icon button plus Ctrl+F, and Escape closes it — the dialog is a sibling of the shell chrome, not inside it
masterSearch.dataStateOwner: BlancShell `masterSearchOpen` component state; the RESULTS are read live across the collected-tools store, saved words, deck cards, dictionary history, grammar points and the library — nothing about the search itself is persisted

contextTools.feature: The Context tools disclosure's declared state and its rendered state move together
contextTools.keyboardRoute: a real disclosure button carrying `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` — an `aria-expanded` that lies is a capability a screen-reader user is told about and cannot reach
contextTools.dataStateOwner: BlancShell `compactToolsOpen` component state — not persisted, so the disclosure is shut on every open

workspaceToggleHonest.feature: The fullscreen-workspace control's label describes the state it would move to, and its exit affordance agrees
workspaceToggleHonest.currentRoute: Blanc window > `#blanc-top-context` > `.blanc-icon-btn` titled "Fullscreen workspace" / "Exit fullscreen workspace", against `.blanc-root.is-workspace-full` and the `.blanc-fullscreen-exit` affordance. It is ROUTE-SCOPED: `canExpandWorkspace` (BlancShell.tsx:430) is `book || tab is one of mine/flashcards/media/stats/tools`, so on Read with no book open the control is deliberately absent and the row reads it on the route the drive visited instead.
workspaceToggleHonest.keyboardRoute: a titled icon button inside the Context tools disclosure; the title is the only thing that says which way the toggle goes
workspaceToggleHonest.dataStateOwner: BlancShell `workspaceFull` component state, whose effect calls `window.api.blancSetFullScreen()` — so the real OS window's fullscreen is downstream of it. That native, persisted side effect is exactly why this row is READ and never DRIVEN.

shellIdentity.feature: Blanc's own material identity is real, and the Study OS desktop is not painting underneath it
shellIdentity.currentRoute: Blanc window > `[data-lq-role="liquid"]` regions — `.blanc-taskbar` and `.blanc-top`, the two the shell owns — with `.os-desktop` required ABSENT from the same document
shellIdentity.keyboardRoute: not a control; it is the shell's claim about which of the two shells the user is in
shellIdentity.dataStateOwner: structural, from BlancShell.tsx. `blancMain.tsx` additionally strips `data-materials` on boot and keeps a MutationObserver on it, so a Study OS material pack cannot leak into this window.

games.standardDestination: Game Arena window, in-window `.game-arena`: the game list down the left, the stage head and its level/language/high-score chips, the two coverage bars, the ready panel with its length note and settings disclosure, the recent-rounds history, and the round shell that replaces the ready panel once a round starts
games.liquidDestination: The same in-window `.game-arena` on the liquid material — `.fwin-liquid` + `data-presentation="liquid"`. SELECTIVE and already built that way: §11's Games split puts the post-round detail and the coverage read-outs on `ContextualSurface` seams (GameArenaContent.tsx:455 and the coverage sections) while the gameplay canvas, the answer box and the history list stay plain opaque bodies — a list of your own last rounds is a table, and L2 keeps tables on stable anchors.

gameCatalog.feature: Browse the game catalogue and select one, with exactly one selected and every entry named and blurbed
gameCatalog.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-list-item` (one per available game), each with its own `small` blurb; `active` marks the selection
gameCatalog.keyboardRoute: real `<button>`s in the window's focus order
gameCatalog.dataStateOwner: component state (`selected`) in GameArenaContent.tsx over `GAME_DEFINITIONS`; the arcade entries are filtered in only once the Aero or Wired theme has been discovered (renderer/aeroDiscovery.ts, renderer/wiredDiscovery.ts), so the catalogue length is a fact about this profile, not a constant

stageIdentity.feature: The stage names the game the list says is selected, and its description is that game's own
stageIdentity.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-stage-head h3` and `.game-stage-head p.muted`, cross-checked against the `active` `.game-list-item`
stageIdentity.keyboardRoute: not a control; it is the surface stating its selection in two places, which is what makes a stale stage detectable
stageIdentity.dataStateOwner: derived from the same `selected` state — nothing separate is stored, so a disagreement is the surface lying to itself

sourceMaterial.feature: Deck coverage for this level: a labelled bar whose fill agrees with the number beside it, and which says so plainly when there is no word list at all
sourceMaterial.currentRoute: Game Arena window > the `.game-coverage` section that is NOT `.game-seen` > its label, note and `.game-coverage-bar i` inline scale
sourceMaterial.keyboardRoute: not a control; a labelled progress read-out
sourceMaterial.dataStateOwner: renderer/games/contentStore.ts `levelCoverage(level)` over the level word lists (renderer/levelLists.ts, localStorage `jp-level-lists` as the synchronous startup cache). An empty profile is HONEST STATE here — "No word list uploaded for this level" with a zero-width bar, not a hidden section.

exposureTracking.feature: Items seen: the stated percentage, the derived percentage and the bar fill are the same number three times
exposureTracking.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-seen` > its stated `pct`, its `seen/total` counts and the `.game-coverage-bar i` inline scale
exposureTracking.keyboardRoute: not a control; a progress read-out that cross-checks itself
exposureTracking.dataStateOwner: renderer/games/seenProgress.ts — localStorage `jp-game-arena-seen-v1`, updated by `markItemSeen` as rounds are played

typingInput.feature: Start a round, type an answer, and have submit unlock — then abort back to a ready state that is really ready
typingInput.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-launch-panel > .btn.primary` starts; `.game-answer-box` takes the answer; `.game-round .btn.primary` is the submit whose `disabled` must move; abort returns to `.game-launch-panel` with no `.game-round-shell`
typingInput.keyboardRoute: a real text input and real buttons; submit's `disabled` is the declared state of "you have not answered yet"
typingInput.dataStateOwner: the round session lives in component state built by `buildGameRound` (renderer/games/engine.ts) and is deliberately NOT persisted — an aborted round leaves nothing behind, which is what makes the abort recovery safe to drive

scoreHud.feature: The round HUD is labelled and its round total equals the session length the ready panel promised
scoreHud.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-round-hud > span` (labelled, with a `.game-time-bar` carrying `aria-valuenow`), cross-checked against the `.game-launch-panel > .muted` session-length note
scoreHud.keyboardRoute: not controls; the HUD is the round stating its own progress, and `aria-valuenow` is how a screen reader gets the timer
scoreHud.dataStateOwner: renderer/games/settings.ts `gameLength` — localStorage `jp-game-arena-settings-v1`; the round list is built to that length, so the HUD total and the note are the same setting rendered twice

roundHistory.feature: Recent rounds are shown back to the player, with an honest empty state when there are none
roundHistory.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-history` > `h4` heading, `.game-history-row` entries or the `.game-history-empty` note
roundHistory.keyboardRoute: not controls; an ordered list read in the ready state, which is the one moment the stage has nothing else to say
roundHistory.dataStateOwner: renderer/stats.ts — localStorage `jp-game-progress-v1` keeps the last 30 results; the panel filters them to the selected game and shows at most 12. Every finished round was already persisted here and nothing had ever shown it back to the player.

materialScope.feature: The kana material picker: choose a scope, and the shape of the selection holds across the choice
materialScope.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-kana-picker` > its mode row and script/group buttons; the chosen mode and the counts it implies are read back together

levelSettings.feature: The stage meta chips (level, language, high score) stay stable across a game switch, and the settings disclosure is a real route into them
levelSettings.currentRoute: Game Arena window > `.game-stage-meta > span` chips, plus `.game-ready-options` and its `.game-ready-options-body > button` entry into Settings
levelSettings.keyboardRoute: a `<details>` disclosure with a real button inside — the chips are read-outs, the entry is the route
levelSettings.dataStateOwner: level from renderer/levelService.ts (`getUserLevel`), language and length from `jp-game-arena-settings-v1`, high score from `jp-game-progress-v1` keyed by game+level+sourceLang. Switching the GAME must not move any of them, which is what this row checks.

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle — Liquid on/off is reversible
windowLifecycle.currentRoute: Game Arena `.fwin` title bar > Make Liquid / Return to standard, plus minimize/maximize/close
windowLifecycle.keyboardRoute: the chrome buttons are in the window's focus order
